feature: Fill the Row: one key gives a piece the room its stack has left
summary: Telling a piece in a stack to take whatever room the stack has left over used to mean opening the panel and picking it out of a menu. It is now one row in the Layer menu with Option F on it, named after the stack it is about, and pressing it a second time gives the piece back the size it had.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Auto layout is on by default, so there is nothing to switch on.

try.do: Draw three rectangles side by side on a blank canvas.
Select all three and press Control Command G to stack them into a row.
With the row still picked, type 700 into W in Position & Size and press Return.
Double click the middle rectangle to pick it inside the row.
Open the Layer menu and read the row under Grid Selection: it should say Fill the Row, on Option F.
Press Option F. The middle rectangle should take everything the other two and the gaps leave.
Press Option F again. It should go back to the 100 points it was drawn at.
Click a rectangle that is not in any stack and open the Layer menu: the row should be grey, and hovering it should say why.

evaluate: Is Option F the key your fingers reach for, sitting beside Option A and the rest of the align set?
Does the row belong under Stack Selection and Grid Selection, or would you look for it beside Align?
Reading Fill the Row in the menu and Fill the row in the Layout section, do they read as one control in two places?
When it is grey, is a hover tip enough of an explanation, or do you want the reason on the row itself?
With three pieces picked at once, is turning them all on with one press what you expected, or did you want it to flip each one?
rough: The row renames itself: Fill the Row inside a row, Fill the Stack inside a column, and Fill the Stack when nothing is picked and it is grey. That last one is a guess at the least misleading name for a dead row, not a considered answer.

Option F is taken by the menu even while the keyboard is in a text field, so it cannot type a florin sign there. The align set already works this way, so this is consistent rather than new, but it is a real cost.

Photographing the menu row live is not possible from the loop: macOS leaves a background app's window menus frozen at their launch state, so the shots here show the canvas and the panel, and the menu row plus its Option F was read out of the probe's own menu bar instead. The grey states and their reasons are covered by 21 PhotonzCore tests rather than a picture.

One thing the menu does that the panel does not: a piece that was filling and is then stretched both ways keeps a rule that now does nothing, and the panel's fill row disappears, so there is nothing left to switch it off with. The menu row stays live whenever a piece is already filling, so taking it off is always reachable.
